newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada banks disappointed with special bank tax.
newsitem.headline: Canada banks disappointed with special bank tax.

text.p: Canada's profitable major banks said on Tuesday they are disappointed Federal Finance Minister Paul Martin extended a special bank tax for another year.
The federal government plans to extend the tax until October 31, 1998, Martin said as he presented his fiscal 1997 budget on Tuesday.
The 12 percent capital tax surcharge on large deposit-taking institutions, introduced in the 1995 budget, is currently scheduled to expire on October 31, 1997.
"Canadian banks are almost certainly the highest taxed industry in Canada," said Raymond Protti, president of the Canadian Bankers Association.
However, the CBA supported the government's strong commitment to balance the budget, which it said is essential to fiscal stability and sustainable economic growth.
